body:
I am thinking this is due to : https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110261

That change reduces based on an `equals` check, relying on that to be overridden correctly. 

I am not sure categorize text is doing this, nor do I believe this is true for all aggs. 

we need to validate this.

Yep, its @original-brownbear 's change showed that we are not appropriately overriding equals/hashcode for categorize text. 

This makes me worry that this isn't the only agg where this is the case :/

A very quick audit shows more than one agg does not override equals. This doesn't just seem like a categorize_text bug. We need to make sure all do and all check their bucket equality, I see some subclassing, but we need to make sure this aggs are overriding equals and checking their buckets.

For example:

 - CategorizeText & timeseries don't override at all
 - InternalRareStringTerms sub-classes a class that does override equals, but doesn't check for bucket equality.

@original-brownbear did you do an audit of aggs overriding equals and checking their sub-bucket equality when you made your original change?
I'm going to spend the morning reproducing this with a debugger so I can describe the mechanism of action for the bug.

Ok. I can reproduce this issue and it does look like it's related to [this](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/110261/files#diff-005547c90c34d3d0a232504d02049fc07827f83a7b331c969d1f51eac919a095R247) filter here. Just like @benwtrent says.

> A very quick audit shows more than one agg does not override equals.

This is critical, but for those following along at home, in java if you don't override `equals` things are *unequal* by default. I presume this is what @original-brownbear assumed would happen. Alas, we [flipped](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/search/aggregations/InternalAggregation.java#L256) this so aggs are considered equal to each other if their name and metadata are equal by default. I believe it's been like this since 2019 in #43214. Like Ben says, for Armin's change to work equality needs to be correct on all aggregations and you can forget that, given how things stand now.

I'll update when I know more.
